prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Companion Status: Playful | Energy: 100% | Ready for Desktop Spawn"]
1: ["Choose Your Pet's Desktop Habitat", "Select the favorite desktop corner or resting zone for your new pet.", "Select Habitat"]
2: ["Master Desktop Pet Controls", "Use quick shortcuts to call, minimize, or feed your pet anywhere on your screen.", "Press Alt+P to hide/show pet"]
3: ["Preview Pet Sound Effects"]
4: ["Configure Pet Personality Traits", "Pick behavioral traits that determine how your pet interacts on your desktop.", "Select Traits"]
5: ["Safeguard Your Desktop Pet", "Sign in to save your pet's appearance, personality, and progress safely in the cloud so your companion is never lost or reset."]
6: []
7: ["Desktop Companion Quick Guide", "Everything you need to know to interact with, feed, and manage your pet on your desktop.", "Right-click pet for menu | Double-click to pet | Drag to move across screen"]
8: ["Use a clear, well-lit photo with a single subject facing forward for best pet rendering results."]
9: ["Initializing desktop graphics and sound engine..."]
